attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: This does not prove that such Q_N exists, and it does not turn sparse or nonconstructive certificates into barriers. It only gives a valid no-go for dense, constructive, same-model label certificates.
steps: Fix N and L=(log N)^d, d>=1; enumerate U_N label-free and define R_L(f)=Q_N(f|U_N).
For uniformly random truth table f on {0,1}^L, the restriction f|U_N is uniform over {0,1}^{U_N}; hence density is exactly preserved as delta_N.
Given a truth table for f, enumerate U_N, read the indexed bits, and run Q_N; the total time is 2^{O(L)} under |U_N|<=N^q.
If R_L(f)=1 and f had size L^c, substitute that circuit into the XOR carrier to get C_N(H_{f|U_N})<=N^{max{q,rho}+o(1)}<N^{1+epsilon}, contradicting Q_N soundness.
Since Q_N accepts SAT|U_N, R_L accepts SAT_L; thus any classically large constructive Q_N would naturalize the proof-mediated source lower bound.

Membership in Q_N from the indexed label table y is decidable in time 2^{O(L)} after enumerating U_N; the enumeration is independent of SAT truth values.
The restriction extension is R_L(f)=1 iff Q_N(f restricted to U_N)=1 for arbitrary Boolean functions f:{0,1}^L -> {0,1}.
definitions: source object: H_y on N-bit source inputs is the XOR carrier H_y(x)=xor_{j<=N^q} y_{G_{N,j}(x)}, where y is a label table on the generated formula range U_N subseteq {0,1}^L and G_N has circuit size N^rho.

controlled interface: beta=0 black-box substitution uses L=(log N)^d with fixed d>=1, substitutes a size L^c circuit for the label oracle y, and pays N^q slot cost plus N^rho generator cost.

steps: Start with a proof-mediated verifier V for CC(TT(SAT_m))>m^k and a candidate accepting seed cluster C of size d.
Define P_C(f) by existentially assigning only the proof cells touched by C, not the full long proof.
If SAT has one proof accepting all seeds in C, then all tables matching SAT on the Q_C queried locations are accepted, giving density at least 2^{-Q_C}.
If B_C=O(log N), P_C is decidable in poly(N) by enumerating the local proof-cell assignments.
Usefulness is equivalent to direct cluster-shadow soundness: no m^k-size circuit truth table has any consistent accepting local proof assignment on C.
Trying to replace direct cluster-shadow soundness by ordinary global-proof soundness fails because the accepting local proof assignment may be chosen after seeing C.
A random-cluster repair needs a shadow cap alpha and yields the threshold log(1/alpha)>=Omega(qm^{k-1} log m) under qd=O(log N).

steps: Fix a claimed hard row T_m and choose block length B=2^{lambda m}; write the input x as block index j and offset r.
For each summary coordinate t, build a multiplexer M_t(j) with the t-th bits of all summaries a_j hardwired. The total selector size is O(q|a_j|)=2^{(1-lambda+mu)m+o(m)}.
Feed the selected summary vector and offset r into one common opener O_m. Circuit sharing avoids copying O_m once per block, so the opener contributes only 2^{omega m+o(m)} gates.
The resulting circuit computes every bit of T_m and has exponent alpha_sem=max{1-lambda+mu,omega}. If alpha_sem<theta, this contradicts the source's MCSP no-side claim.
Checkpoint, skip-ahead, block-digest, Merkle-opening, and rankable block-summary implementations instantiate the same cover once their summaries and openers are expressible as nonuniform circuits.
Trying to promote the route now requires proving that a generated anti-ball row has no semantic cover below theta, not merely that the generator is sequential or noniteratable.

The argument is a route-level falsifier for MCSP carrier soundness, not a proof of P != NP or a natural-property lower bound.
definitions: source object: a generated anti-ball MCSP carrier row T_m in {0,1}^{2^m}, intended to be a truth table of an m-bit Boolean function with unrestricted circuit complexity above 2^{theta m}.
target object: an E language L obtained from canonical row/image multiplexing and kappa-gap padding, intended to inherit SIZE(2^{delta n}) lower bounds from the hard row.

controlled interface: a semantic block cover with block exponent lambda, summary exponent mu, and opener exponent omega: q=2^{(1-lambda)m} blocks, summaries a_j of length at most 2^{mu m+o(m)}, and one common circuit O_m of size 2^{omega m+o(m)} opening any bit from the selected summary.

target-preserving condition: the carrier-to-E extraction is valid only for an advice-free canonically located row whose semantic-cover exponent is at least theta-o(1), with image entropy D and kappa-gap padding preserved; a subtheta cover is a nonuniform circuit upper bound and kills the source.

equations.label: block_count
equations.valid_when: Valid when T_m is viewed as a truth table on m variables and the chosen block partition has exponential block length 2^{lambda m}.

equations.label: semantic_cover_upper_bound
equations.valid_when: Valid when all block summaries can be hardwired and one common opener circuit can be shared after multiplexing the selected summary bits.

equations.label: falsifier_threshold
equations.valid_when: Valid when the source claim is an unrestricted MCSP no-side claim at threshold 2^{theta m} for the same row T_m.

equations.label: surviving_extraction_rate
equations.valid_when: Applies after the row survives the semantic-cover audit and the canonical multiplexing preserves image entropy D, padding gap kappa, and E-uniform location.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: Exhibit, for the proposed source row, block summaries and a common opener with alpha_sem<theta. This includes checkpoint streams, commitment openings, affine skip-ahead streams, and any proof skeleton that supports subthreshold block recovery.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Finite falsifier and validation gate for generated anti-ball carriers; it sharpens the block-summary-hard obligation without changing the conditional extraction theorem.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Semantic block-cover gate: if a claimed MCSP-hard carrier row T_m has a block decomposition whose blocks have short summaries and a common small opener, then T_m has a small unrestricted circuit. Hence any source claiming CC(T_m)>2^{theta m} is invalid when the cover exponent is below theta.

assumptions: Distinct-image entropy is bounded by Dm+o(m), and duplicate certificates are quotiented by an E-canonical image ranking.
The row/proof generator may be sequential and long, but the extracted row bit must be computable in E time at the padded target length.
No density repair is allowed that turns the sparse source into a polynomial-time decidable large useful property.

Validity/model regime: this lemma is interpreted only within the stated P vs NP branch model, with the same source object, target object, circuit class, length regime, and advice/uniformity assumptions used by the branch output.
definitions: source object: a sparse generated family of row/proof streams producing at least one candidate row T_m in every kappa-gap interval.
target object: the multiplexed E language whose input first selects a canonical distinct image and then evaluates the row bit.
bridge object: the semantic covering dimension covdim_m(T), which records the best nonuniform block-summary opening upper bound for the row.
observable: whether the claimed anti-ball proof excludes all unrestricted circuits below 2^{theta m}, including those built from semantic block summaries.

equations.label: cover_dimension
equations.valid_when: Valid when C(T) denotes the set of semantic block covers using exponentially parameterized block length, summary length, and opener size.

equations.label: necessary_source_condition
equations.valid_when: Valid when the semantic cover upper bound is measured in the same unrestricted nonuniform circuit model as the MCSP threshold.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A source theorem that proves only sequential generation, noniterability, or anti-skip behavior but not covdim_m(T)>=theta-o(1) remains vulnerable to the semantic-cover falsifier.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Turns the latest leakage audits into one named necessary invariant for source proposals.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Define covdim_m(T) as the infimum of alpha_sem over all semantic block covers of T. A generated MCSP source with threshold theta must certify covdim_m(T)>=theta-o(1) for its selected hard rows before the usual low-D carrier extraction is valid.

control_decision.pivot_test: Backtrack if every plausible generated anti-ball source yields alpha_sem<theta under a natural block partition, or if proving covdim>=theta is equivalent to assuming the target lower bound.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote if a named proof system gives an advice-free generated certificate that covdim_m(T)>=theta-o(1) for kappa-dense rows while preserving D=O(1) and E-canonical location.
control_decision.reason: The branch made route-level progress by turning block-summary leakage into an exact finite falsifier, but the source theorem remains open and likely circular without a sparse non-natural certificate of high covdim.

dependency_updates.description: Carrier soundness now requires high semantic covering dimension, not just anti-skip, anti-checkpoint, or sequential generation.
The valid extraction rate remains delta<theta/(kappa(1+D)) once a row is genuinely MCSP-hard and canonically located.
Explicit generation must not create block summaries or common openers below the claimed threshold, even if those objects are not efficiently findable.
Compare the semantic block-cover gate with known self-reducibility, instance compression, MCSP, and time-space checkpoint upper-bound arguments.

falsifiers: falsifier: a block commitment or proof stream with summaries of exponent mu and common opener exponent omega satisfying max{1-lambda+mu,omega}<theta.
falsifier: polynomial-space near-linear sequential generation with checkpoint summaries giving the earlier theta>1/2 cap as a special case.
falsifier: algebraic skip-ahead or iteratable transitions that yield block summaries with subtheta openers even if the full stream looks globally sequential.
falsifier: dense locator or projection repair that makes a polynomial-time decidable large useful property while preserving small-circuit exclusion.
falsifier: unbounded distinct-image entropy D, which leaves the source perhaps hard nonuniformly but destroys the stated E-transfer exponent.

gedanken_experiment_design.expected_observation: Ordinary commitment or checkpoint implementations should show alpha_sem(lambda)=max{1-lambda+mu(lambda),omega(lambda)} dropping below theta for large enough lambda, giving a finite invalidation. A viable source must force either mu(lambda)>=theta+lambda-1 or omega(lambda)>=theta for every lambda.
held_fixed_controls: Keep the target extraction model fixed: E-uniform canonical row/image multiplexing with image entropy D and padding gap kappa.
Keep the source hardness claim fixed: unrestricted MCSP no-side threshold 2^{theta m}, not uniform or restricted-circuit hardness.
Keep the source sparse and advice-free so that natural-property largeness and nonuniform row-choice leakage are not introduced.
gedanken_experiment_design.rationale: The branch needs a concrete falsifier probe for generated anti-ball sources: sequentiality and noniterability are too weak unless they exclude semantic block covers in the unrestricted circuit model.
gedanken_experiment_design.situation_seed: Take a generated anti-ball MCSP row/proof stream whose proof is organized into block commitments. The row length is N=2^m, the claimed hardness threshold is 2^{theta m}, and each block has a generated certificate opening all bits in that block.
gedanken_experiment_design.transfer_certificate_needed: Before the intuition can affect proof obligations, prove a semantic-cover lower bound covdim_m(T)>=theta-o(1) for the selected row and verify that canonical extraction still has delta<theta/(kappa(1+D)) in E.
gedanken_experiment_design.varied_variable: Vary the block length exponent lambda while measuring the induced summary exponent mu(lambda) and opener exponent omega(lambda).

branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 70 compresses several leakage channels into a single semantic block-cover exponent. Any generated MCSP carrier whose row admits short per-block summaries and a shared opener has an unrestricted circuit of exponent alpha_sem=max{1-lambda+mu,omega}. Thus a valid source must prove high semantic covering dimension; sequential, noniteratable, or advice-free generation alone is insufficient.
